gap: The paper never defines how the 'primary emoji' of a tweet is chosen when a tweet contains several emojis, yet this determines the per-emoji tweet sets T_e and hence every delta value.
options: first emoji in the raw tweet (consistent with the placement analysis, which classifies by the first emoji)
last emoji in the tweet (sentence-final dominance)
most frequent / nearest-to-end emoji
one row per (tweet, emoji) pair, allowing multi-membership
chosen: first emoji in the raw tweet after canonicalisation
rationale: Section 4.2 explicitly classifies placement by the position of the first emoji, so using the first emoji keeps the primary-emoji definition consistent with the rest of the paper.

gap: The random draws (up to 100 tweets per emoji, 500 background tweets, bootstraps) need a random seed that the paper never states.
options: fixed seed 42 for every draw
seed 0
average over several seeds
chosen: fixed seed 42 for the sampling draws and the bootstrap/permutation resampling
rationale: 42 is the only seed the paper prints (for the CV splits), so reusing it is the most defensible single choice; a single fixed seed must be recorded for exact reproducibility.

gap: The variance of (p_neg, p_neu, p_pos) is not specified as population or sample variance.

sample variance (ddof = 1)
rationale: The three probabilities are treated as the complete distribution for the emoji, not a sample of it; the subsequent Spearman test is rank-based so the choice barely moves rho.

gap: How per-emoji scalars should be read out of the emosent-py package (which column is the 'sentiment score', and how probabilities are ordered).
